set_title: Pericarditis vs endocarditis names: which layer and what is growing on the valve
stem: A 60-year-old man with metastatic pancreatic adenocarcinoma has sudden right-sided weakness and aphasia. Blood cultures are negative. Echocardiography shows small friable growths along the closure line of the mitral valve, without valve destruction.
oneliner: 60-year-old man, pancreatic cancer, embolic stroke, sterile small valve growths → ?

whyNot.A: Needs fever and positive cultures; his **blood cultures are negative** with no destruction
whyNot.B: Occurs in lupus; he has **metastatic pancreatic cancer** and no SLE features
whyNot.C: Follows strep in children with arthritis; he is **60 with metastatic cancer**
whyNot.D: Causes Kussmaul sign and edema; he has **embolic stroke from valve growths**

why: Marantic comes from the Greek for wasting: sterile clots on valves in cancer. **Cancer, negative cultures and embolic stroke** fit.

head: Term
Means
One clue
rows: **Pain better leaning forward; diffuse ST elevation**
**Advanced cancer; sterile clots on closure line**
post-strep inflammation of all heart layers

idea.rule: Marantic = wasting; sterile growths on the valve closure line in cancer.

set_title: Thrombo- names: clots vs too few or too many platelets
stem: A 25-year-old woman has 2 days of fever, confusion and petechiae. Platelets are 18,000/mm3, hemoglobin 8 g/dL and creatinine 1.8 mg/dL. The smear shows fragmented red cells; PT and PTT are normal.
oneliner: 25-year-old woman, fever, confusion, schistocytes, low platelets, normal PT → ?

whyNot.A: Isolated low platelets; she has **fragmented red cells, fever and confusion**
whyNot.B: Needs recent heparin and clots; she has **schistocytes with renal and neurologic signs**
whyNot.E: Cancer-linked moving vein clots; she has **hemolysis with low platelets**

why: Clots (thrombotic) in small vessels consume platelets (thrombocytopenia) and cause purpura. **Fever, confusion, schistocytes and normal PT** indicate low ADAMTS13.

head: Term
Means
One clue
rows: **Recurrent clots in different veins; pancreatic cancer**

idea.rule: TTP = schistocytes plus low platelets with normal PT; ITP has a clean smear.
also: Pentad: fever, confusion, kidney, anemia, platelets

set_title: Thrombo- names: clots vs too few or too many platelets
stem: A 62-year-old man had hip replacement and was started on an infusion that potentiates antithrombin III 7 days ago. His platelets fell from 240,000 to 105,000/mm3, and he now has a swollen left calf with a deep vein thrombosis on ultrasound.
oneliner: 62-year-old man, day 7 of antithrombin-potentiating infusion, platelets halved, new DVT → ?

whyNot.A: Needs schistocytes, fever and confusion; he has **platelets falling on day 7 with DVT**
whyNot.C: Bleeds, not clots; he has a **new deep vein thrombosis**
whyNot.D: Platelets are high; his **fell from 240,000 to 105,000/mm3**
whyNot.E: Occurs with cancer; his drop followed **7 days of the infusion**

why: Heparin antibodies against platelet factor 4 activate platelets: low count, paradoxical clots. **Platelets halving around day 7 with a new DVT** is classic.

head: Term
Means
One clue
rows: **Recurrent clots in different veins; pancreatic cancer**

idea.rule: Heparin plus falling platelets plus clots = HIT; stop heparin, start a non-heparin anticoagulant.

set_title: Thrombo- names: clots vs too few or too many platelets
stem: A 5-year-old boy has petechiae and bruises 2 weeks after a viral upper respiratory infection. He is otherwise well. Platelets are 15,000/mm3, with normal hemoglobin and leukocyte count; the smear shows large platelets and no fragmented red cells.
oneliner: 5-year-old boy, petechiae 2 weeks after a cold, platelets 15,000, otherwise normal → ?

whyNot.A: Needs schistocytes, fever and confusion; he is **otherwise well with a clean smear**
whyNot.B: Needs heparin exposure and clots; he has **petechiae after a viral illness**
whyNot.E: Cancer-related clots; he is a **well 5-year-old with bleeding**

why: Immune antibodies destroy platelets (thrombocytopenia). **Isolated low platelets, large platelets and a clean smear after a viral illness** are typical.

head: Term
Means
One clue
rows: **Recurrent clots in different veins; pancreatic cancer**

idea.rule: ITP = isolated low platelets, clean smear; TTP adds schistocytes and organ injury.

set_title: Von- names: von Gierke, von Hippel-Lindau, von Recklinghausen (two of them), von Willebrand
stem: A 17-year-old girl has heavy menstrual bleeding and frequent nosebleeds. Platelet count and PT are normal, PTT is mildly prolonged, bleeding time is prolonged, and ristocetin-induced platelet aggregation is reduced. Her father has similar bleeding.
oneliner: 17-year-old girl, heavy periods, nosebleeds, long bleeding time, reduced ristocetin response → ?

options.B: Von Gierke disease (glycogen storage type I)
options.E: Osteitis fibrosa cystica (von Recklinghausen disease of bone)

whyNot.B: Causes fasting hypoglycemia and hepatomegaly; she has **mucosal bleeding and long bleeding time**
whyNot.C: Causes hemangioblastomas and renal cancer; she has **mucosal bleeding and reduced ristocetin response**
whyNot.D: Causes cafe-au-lait spots; she has **heavy menses and long bleeding time**
whyNot.E: Needs high PTH and bone pain; she has **mucosal bleeding with normal platelets**

why: Von Willebrand factor carries factor VIII and bridges platelets to collagen; low levels cause bleeding. **Mucosal bleeding, long bleeding time, low ristocetin response** fit.

head: Term
Means
One clue
rows: Von Gierke disease (glycogen storage type I)
Osteitis fibrosa cystica (von Recklinghausen disease of bone)
inflamed fibrous cystic bone from high PTH

idea.rule: Mucosal bleeding with normal platelets and abnormal ristocetin = von Willebrand disease.
also: vWF protects factor VIII, so PTT rises

set_title: Ka- names: Kawasaki, Kaposi, Kasabach-Merritt, Kartagener, Kallmann
stem: A 35-year-old man with HIV (CD4 count 80/mm3) has several painless purple-red plaques and nodules on the legs and hard palate. Biopsy shows spindle cells forming slit-like vascular spaces with extravasated red blood cells.
oneliner: 35-year-old man, HIV, purple nodules on legs, spindle cells and slit-like spaces → ?

whyNot.A: Causes fever and coronary aneurysm in children; he has **skin tumors in HIV**
whyNot.C: Infant vascular tumor with low platelets; he has **HIV and spindle cell nodules**
whyNot.D: Causes sinusitis and dextrocardia; he has **purple vascular nodules**
whyNot.E: Causes absent puberty and anosmia; he has **purple vascular nodules in HIV**

why: Named for Moritz Kaposi: an HHV-8 vascular tumor. **Purple nodules in advanced HIV with spindle cells and slit-like vascular spaces** fit.

head: Term
Means
One clue
rows: eponym: platelets trapped in vascular tumor
eponym: ciliary dyskinesia with situs inversus
eponym: GnRH neurons fail to migrate

idea.rule: Purple skin nodules in AIDS with spindle cells = Kaposi sarcoma; HHV-8 (KSHV).

set_title: Horner vs Homer Wright: a droopy-eye syndrome vs a tumor rosette (and other pupils and rosettes)
stem: A 2-year-old boy has a firm abdominal mass that crosses the midline and rapid jerking movements of his eyes. Urine vanillylmandelic acid is high. Biopsy shows small blue cells arranged around a center of pink fibrils with no lumen.
oneliner: 2-year-old boy, abdominal mass + opsoclonus + high urine VMA + small blue cells around fibrils, no lumen → ?
ask: Which term names the biopsy pattern?

whyNot.A: Horner syndrome is a clinical triad; his clue is a **biopsy pattern around fibrils**
whyNot.C: Argyll Robertson pupil is a syphilis sign, not a **biopsy pattern**
whyNot.D: Marcus Gunn pupil is an optic-nerve sign, not a **biopsy pattern**
whyNot.E: Flexner-Wintersteiner rosettes have a true lumen (retinoblastoma); his surround **fibrils, no lumen**

why: Rosettes of cells around a core of neuropil fibrils, with no true lumen. **Small blue cells around fibrils with no lumen** in a child with high VMA is neuroblastoma.

head: Term
Means
One clue
rows: **Swinging light to bad eye: both dilate**
tumor cells around fibrils, no lumen

idea.rule: Homer Wright: no lumen (neuroblastoma); Flexner-Wintersteiner: true lumen (retinoblastoma).

set_title: Leuko- names: white patches, a white pupil, white cells and white matter
stem: A 65-year-old man who has chewed tobacco for 40 years has a painless patch inside his cheek that cannot be scraped off. Biopsy shows hyperkeratosis with epithelial dysplasia.
oneliner: 65-year-old man, 40 years of chewing tobacco + painless cheek patch that will not scrape off + dysplasia → ?

whyNot.A: Oral hairy leukoplakia is on the tongue side; his patch is on the **cheek**
whyNot.C: Leukocoria is a pupil sign in children; he has a **cheek patch**
whyNot.D: Leukemoid reaction is a blood count finding; his problem is a **cheek patch**
whyNot.E: Progressive multifocal leukoencephalopathy is a brain disease; he has a **mucosal patch with dysplasia**

why: Leuko (white) + plakia (plate): a white mucosal plaque that cannot be wiped off. **Tobacco use and dysplasia** make it premalignant, so biopsy any one.

head: Term
Means
One clue
rows: **White oral patch that won't scrape off**
many foci + white matter + brain disease

idea.rule: Leukoplakia cannot be scraped off; candida thrush can.

set_title: Leuko- names: white patches, a white pupil, white cells and white matter
stem: An 18-month-old girl's parents notice that in flash photographs her left eye glows pale instead of red. She has no fever, no pain and no redness of the eye.
oneliner: 18-month-old girl, flash photos show pale left pupil glow instead of red + no pain or redness → ?

whyNot.A: Leukoplakia is a mucosal patch; her finding is an **abnormal pupil reflex in photographs**
whyNot.B: Oral hairy leukoplakia is a tongue lesion; her finding is an **eye reflex change**
whyNot.D: Leukemoid reaction is a high white count; hers is a **pupil sign**
whyNot.E: Progressive multifocal leukoencephalopathy needs immunosuppression and brain signs; she has an **abnormal pupil reflex**

why: Leuko (white) + core (pupil): an abnormal reflex from a retinal mass or cataract. **A pale pupil reflex in flash photographs** needs urgent exclusion of retinoblastoma.

head: Term
Means
One clue
rows: **White oral patch that won't scrape off**
many foci + white matter + brain disease

idea.rule: Leukocoria = white pupil, any cause; retinoblastoma is the one to exclude.
also: Cataract, retinal detachment also cause it

set_title: Fanconi anemia vs Fanconi syndrome and other aplasia names
stem: A 7-year-old boy is short and has absent thumbs and café-au-lait spots. Blood counts show low hemoglobin, white cells and platelets. Chromosome breaks increase after exposure to a DNA cross-linking agent.
oneliner: 7-year-old boy, short + absent thumbs + café-au-lait spots + pancytopenia + chromosome breaks → ?

whyNot.A: Fanconi syndrome is a kidney tubule disorder; he has **pancytopenia and absent thumbs**
whyNot.C: Diamond-Blackfan anemia affects only red cells in infancy; he has **pancytopenia at 7**
whyNot.D: Aplastic anemia is acquired and lacks anomalies; he has **absent thumbs and short stature**
whyNot.E: Pure red cell aplasia spares white cells and platelets; he has **pancytopenia**

why: Inherited DNA-repair defect with marrow failure and congenital anomalies. **Pancytopenia, absent thumbs, short stature and chromosome breaks with cross-linkers**; AML risk later.

head: Term
Means
One clue
rows: inherited marrow failure, DNA repair defect

idea.rule: Fanconi anemia = marrow and anomalies; Fanconi syndrome = proximal tubule.
also: Risk of AML and squamous cancers

set_title: Fanconi anemia vs Fanconi syndrome and other aplasia names
stem: A 3-month-old girl is pale. Hemoglobin is 6 g/dL, MCV is high, and reticulocytes are low, with normal white cells and platelets. She has a triphalangeal thumb. Marrow shows few erythroid precursors.
oneliner: 3-month-old girl, pallor + macrocytic anemia + low reticulocytes + normal WBC and platelets + triphalangeal thumb → ?

whyNot.A: Fanconi anemia causes pancytopenia; she has **normal white cells and platelets**
whyNot.C: Transient erythroblastopenia starts after 6 months, no anomalies; she has a **triphalangeal thumb**
whyNot.D: Aplastic anemia has pancytopenia and fatty marrow; she has **normal white cells and platelets**
whyNot.E: Pure red cell aplasia is acquired without anomalies; she has a **triphalangeal thumb**

why: Congenital red-cell aplasia, from ribosomal protein gene mutations. **Infant macrocytic anemia, low reticulocytes, normal other lines and thumb anomaly**; treat with steroids.

head: Term
Means
One clue
rows: inherited marrow failure, DNA repair defect

idea.rule: Diamond-Blackfan: congenital, infant, thumbs; pure red cell aplasia: acquired, adult.

set_title: Fanconi anemia vs Fanconi syndrome and other aplasia names
stem: A 55-year-old man with a thymoma has had fatigue for 2 months. Hemoglobin is 7 g/dL, the reticulocyte count is near zero, and white cell and platelet counts are normal. Marrow shows no erythroid precursors.
oneliner: 55-year-old man, thymoma + anemia + reticulocytes near zero + normal WBC and platelets + no erythroid precursors → ?

whyNot.A: Fanconi anemia causes childhood pancytopenia; he has **isolated anemia at 55**
whyNot.B: Fanconi syndrome is a renal tubular disorder; his marrow has **no erythroid precursors**
whyNot.C: Diamond-Blackfan anemia presents in infancy; he is **55 with a thymoma**
whyNot.D: Aplastic anemia lowers all three lines; his **white cells and platelets are normal**

why: Pure (single line) red cell aplasia: antibodies or parvovirus destroy red precursors. **Isolated anemia, near-zero reticulocytes and a thymoma**; remove the thymoma.

head: Term
Means
One clue
rows: inherited marrow failure, DNA repair defect

idea.rule: Pure red cell aplasia: only red cells vanish; think thymoma, parvovirus.
also: Also parvovirus B19 in sickle cell

set_title: Thalassemia names: alpha vs beta, trait vs major, HbH vs Barts
stem: A 30-year-old Asian woman has mild microcytic anemia (hemoglobin 11 g/dL, MCV 68 fL). Ferritin is normal. Hemoglobin electrophoresis is normal. Her husband has a similar mild microcytic picture.
oneliner: 30-year-old Asian woman, mild microcytic anemia MCV 68 + normal ferritin + normal electrophoresis → ?

whyNot.A: Hemoglobin H disease causes moderate hemolytic anemia; she has **only mild microcytosis**
whyNot.B: Hemoglobin Barts is fatal in utero; she is a **healthy adult with mild anemia**
whyNot.D: Beta-thalassemia minor shows raised HbA2; her **electrophoresis is normal**
whyNot.E: Beta-thalassemia major causes severe transfusion-dependent anemia; her anemia is **mild**

why: Two of four alpha genes deleted, so mild microcytosis with normal iron and a normal electrophoresis. **Mild microcytic anemia, normal ferritin and normal electrophoresis**.

head: Term
Means
One clue
rows: three alpha genes deleted; beta4 tetramers

idea.rule: Count the alpha genes: 1 silent, 2 trait, 3 HbH, 4 Barts.
also: Diagnosis of exclusion with iron deficiency

set_title: Thalassemia names: alpha vs beta, trait vs major, HbH vs Barts
stem: A newborn girl, born at 32 weeks to Southeast Asian parents, has generalized edema, ascites and a large liver and dies within hours. Hemoglobin is 4 g/dL. Electrophoresis shows mostly gamma-chain tetramers.
oneliner: Newborn girl, 32 weeks, Southeast Asian parents + generalized edema and ascites + Hb 4 + gamma tetramers → ?

whyNot.A: Alpha-thalassemia trait causes mild anemia; she has **hydrops and Hb 4**
whyNot.C: Hemoglobin H disease is survivable with beta4; her cells have **gamma tetramers, hydrops**
whyNot.D: Hereditary persistence of fetal hemoglobin is benign; she has **hydrops and Hb 4**
whyNot.E: Beta-thalassemia major appears after 6 months when HbF falls; she has **hydrops at birth**

why: All four alpha genes deleted, so no HbF or HbA; gamma chains form Barts tetramers that cannot release oxygen. **Hydrops and gamma tetramers** are fatal.

head: Term
Means
One clue
rows: three alpha genes deleted; beta4 tetramers

idea.rule: Barts = gamma4, no alpha at all; HbH = beta4 with three alpha deleted.

set_title: Thalassemia names: alpha vs beta, trait vs major, HbH vs Barts
stem: A 25-year-old Greek man has mild microcytic anemia (hemoglobin 11.5 g/dL, MCV 65 fL) found at a routine visit. Ferritin is normal, and the smear shows target cells. Hemoglobin electrophoresis shows HbA2 of 5%.
oneliner: 25-year-old Greek man, mild microcytic anemia MCV 65 + normal ferritin + target cells + HbA2 5% → ?

whyNot.A: Alpha-thalassemia trait has a normal electrophoresis; his **HbA2 is raised at 5%**
whyNot.B: Hemoglobin H disease causes hemolysis with HbH; he has **mild anemia and raised HbA2**
whyNot.C: Hemoglobin Barts is fatal in utero; he is a **healthy 25-year-old**
whyNot.D: Beta-thalassemia major needs transfusions from infancy; his anemia is **mild**

why: One defective beta gene: HbA2 (alpha2 delta2) rises. **Mild microcytic anemia, normal ferritin and HbA2 above 3.5%** is beta-thalassemia minor.

head: Term
Means
One clue
rows: three alpha genes deleted; beta4 tetramers

idea.rule: Beta minor: HbA2 up; alpha trait: electrophoresis normal.

set_title: Thalassemia names: alpha vs beta, trait vs major, HbH vs Barts
stem: An 8-month-old Mediterranean boy has severe pallor, a large spleen and frontal bossing. Hemoglobin is 5 g/dL. Electrophoresis shows mostly HbF with no HbA. Skull x-ray shows a hair-on-end appearance.
oneliner: 8-month-old Mediterranean boy, severe anemia + splenomegaly + frontal bossing + hair-on-end skull + HbF, no HbA → ?

whyNot.A: Alpha-thalassemia trait causes mild anemia; he has **Hb 5 with HbF only**
whyNot.B: Hemoglobin H disease gives moderate anemia with HbH; he has **HbF only, no HbA**
whyNot.D: Hemoglobin Barts causes death in utero; he is **alive at 8 months with HbF**
whyNot.E: Beta-thalassemia minor causes mild anemia; he has **severe anemia and bone changes**

why: Both beta genes defective: no HbA, anemia appears at about 6 months as HbF falls. **Severe anemia, hair-on-end skull and HbF only**; needs transfusion.

head: Term
Means
One clue
rows: three alpha genes deleted; beta4 tetramers

idea.rule: Beta major shows at 6 months, when fetal hemoglobin switches off.

set_title: Esophagus eponyms: Mallory-Weiss, Boerhaave, Barrett, Zenker, Plummer-Vinson
stem: A 45-year-old woman has had 6 months of difficulty swallowing solids. She is fatigued, with a smooth sore tongue and spoon-shaped nails. Hemoglobin is 9 g/dL, MCV is 72 fL, and ferritin is low. Barium swallow shows a thin web in the upper esophagus.
oneliner: 45-year-old woman, dysphagia for solids + smooth sore tongue + spoon nails + iron-deficiency anemia + upper esophageal web → ?

whyNot.A: Mallory-Weiss is an acute tear with hematemesis; she has **chronic dysphagia with iron deficiency**
whyNot.B: Zenker diverticulum causes regurgitation and halitosis; she has **a web and iron-deficiency anemia**
whyNot.C: Eosinophilic esophagitis causes food impaction in atopic men; she has **iron-deficiency anemia, glossitis**
whyNot.D: Mallory bodies are liver-cell inclusions; she has **an esophageal web with iron deficiency**

why: Esophageal web with iron-deficiency anemia and glossitis; increases risk of squamous cell carcinoma. **Dysphagia, spoon nails, low ferritin and an upper esophageal web**.

idea.rule: Plummer-Vinson: web + iron deficiency + dysphagia in middle-aged women.

set_title: Myelo- names: marrow or spinal cord?
stem: A 72-year-old man has 3 months of fatigue and easy bruising. Hemoglobin is 8.9 g/dL with an MCV of 104 fL, the leukocyte count is 2400/mm3, and the platelet count is 60,000/mm3. Vitamin B12 and folate levels are normal. The blood smear shows neutrophils with only two nuclear lobes and few granules. The bone marrow is hypercellular with abnormal-looking precursors, ringed sideroblasts and 6% blasts. The spleen is not enlarged.
oneliner: 72M + macrocytic anemia, low WBC and platelets, normal B12 and folate + bilobed neutrophils + busy marrow, 6% blasts → ?

whyNot.A: Myelofibrosis scars marrow and enlarges the spleen; he has **a hypercellular marrow, no splenomegaly**
whyNot.C: Myeloproliferative neoplasms overproduce mature cells; he has **low counts in all three lines**
whyNot.D: Myelophthisis is marrow crowded by tumor; his is **full of his own dysplastic precursors**
whyNot.E: Myelomeningocele is a spinal cord defect at birth; he is **72 with cytopenias**

why: Marrow + abnormal forming: a busy marrow makes faulty cells. **Macrocytic cytopenias, hypercellular marrow, bilobed neutrophils, ringed sideroblasts, under 20% blasts** is myelodysplastic syndrome.

head: Means
One clue
rows: **Sensory level on trunk with bladder trouble**

idea.rule: Myelodysplastic = busy marrow, low counts; myeloproliferative = busy marrow, high counts.
also: Risks: age over 60, alkylators, radiation, benzene

set_title: Myelo- names: marrow or spinal cord?
stem: A 66-year-old woman has 4 months of fatigue, fullness after small meals, and a 6-kg weight loss. Her spleen is felt 12 cm below the left costal margin. Hemoglobin is 9.5 g/dL. The blood smear shows teardrop-shaped red cells, nucleated red cells and myelocytes. Marrow aspiration yields no cells, and the biopsy shows dense reticulin fibrosis with clusters of atypical megakaryocytes. A JAK2 V617F mutation is found. She has no history of cancer.
oneliner: 66F + early satiety, huge spleen + teardrop cells and nucleated red cells + dry tap with reticulin fibrosis + JAK2 → ?

whyNot.A: Myelodysplastic syndrome has a hypercellular marrow; she has **a dry tap and huge spleen**
whyNot.B: Myelophthisis needs invading cells like cancer; she has **no cancer, JAK2, and fibrosis**
whyNot.D: Transverse myelitis inflames the cord with a sensory level; she has **a huge spleen**
whyNot.E: Myelomeningocele is a neural tube defect at birth; she is **66 with marrow fibrosis**

why: Marrow + scarring: blood is then made in spleen and liver. **Massive spleen, teardrops, dry tap, reticulin fibrosis and JAK2** mean primary myelofibrosis.

head: Means
One clue
rows: **Sensory level on trunk with bladder trouble**

idea.rule: Teardrops + massive spleen + dry tap + JAK2 = myelofibrosis.
also: JAK2, CALR or MPL mutation (an MPN)
Ruxolitinib shrinks the spleen; transplant can cure

set_title: Myelo- names: marrow or spinal cord?
stem: A 61-year-old woman was treated for breast cancer 5 years ago. She now has 2 months of fatigue and low back pain. Hemoglobin is 8.6 g/dL, the leukocyte count is 4000/mm3, and the platelet count is 90,000/mm3. The blood smear shows nucleated red cells, myelocytes and some teardrop cells. Her spleen is not enlarged. A bone marrow biopsy shows clusters of cytokeratin-positive epithelial cells filling the marrow spaces.
oneliner: 61F, past breast cancer + back pain and cytopenias + nucleated red cells and myelocytes on smear + epithelial cells filling the marrow → ?

whyNot.A: Myelofibrosis means fibrosis, huge spleen; she has **no splenomegaly, cancer cells in marrow**
whyNot.B: Myelomeningocele is a congenital cord sac; she is **61 with cytopenias after breast cancer**
whyNot.C: Myelodysplastic syndrome has bilobed neutrophils; her marrow holds **cytokeratin-positive epithelial cells**
whyNot.E: Transverse myelitis causes weakness and a sensory level; she has **cytopenias with marrow tumor**

why: Marrow + wasting away: foreign cells crowd out the marrow. **Leukoerythroblastic smear and cytokeratin-positive cells after breast cancer** is myelophthisis.

head: Means
One clue
rows: **Sensory level on trunk with bladder trouble**

idea.rule: Leukoerythroblastic smear + known cancer + tumor in marrow = myelophthisis.
also: Usual invaders: breast, prostate, lung cancer
TB, fungi and Gaucher disease also can
